stem.text: Cars pass a checkpoint at a rate of C(t) cars per minute, where C is differentiable and t is measured in minutes. Measured values are C(0) = 8, C(5) = 14, C(15) = 20, C(20) = 10. Find the approximation to \( \int_{0}^{20} C(t)\,dt \), the number of cars that pass the checkpoint from t = 0 to t = 20, given by a trapezoidal sum with the three subintervals indicated by these values. Give the exact value.

worked_solution.text: Each subinterval contributes its width times the average of its two endpoint values: \( 5 \cdot \frac{8 + 14}{2} = 55 \); \( 10 \cdot \frac{14 + 20}{2} = 170 \); \( 5 \cdot \frac{20 + 10}{2} = 75 \).

distractor_derivations.A: trapezoidal sum with the common width (b - a)/3 used for every subinterval
distractor_derivations.B: right Riemann sum used in place of the trapezoidal sum
distractor_derivations.C: factor 1/2 applied to the first trapezoid only
